description:
Round-28 perf lever L7 (docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md §A.2 row 6).

=== DONE (s470bp) ===

`@a[1..5]` and `@h{@k}` are ALIASES in perl — `for (@a[0,1]) { $_ *= 10 }`
writes through — so `p-aslice` / `p-hslice` build a vector of the container's
own element CELLS (%p-alias-aelem / %p-alias-helem), which under raw element
storage PROMOTES each slot to a box.  Promotion is MONOTONE: the container then
pays box indirection on every later read, forever, and the boxes are allocated
for nothing.

`my @v = @a[1..5]` needs none of it.  A list assignment COPIES, so the aliases
are unboxed and thrown away one call later.  THE LICENCE IS THE CONSUMER, and
it is decided where the consumer is visible — in `p-array-=`'s macro, whose
VALUE form is syntactically the slice (`%p-copying-slice-form`).  Every other
consumer — a foreach, a `\(…)`, a sub call that may alias — never reaches this
arm and keeps `p-aslice`/`p-hslice` untouched, so the aliasing shapes are
unaffected (probed: `for (@a[0..1]) { $_ *= 10 }` still writes through).

THE READ IS THE EXISTING ONE (rule 11): `%p-aslice-copy` asks `p-aref` and
`%p-hslice-copy` asks `p-gethash` — the runtime's ONE reading of "what is
@a[i] / $h{k} as a VALUE", with negative indices, out-of-range undef, symbolic
refs, magic cells, the box kept for a reference, and the s458ak fast arms.
Asking them is what keeps the copying slice and the element read from ever
disagreeing.

IT ALSO FIXED A DIVERGENCE, which is the sign the licence is the right one:
`my @a=(1,2); my @v=@a[0..3]; exists $v[3]` was FALSE in PCL and TRUE in perl —
the alias path produced something p-array-fill stored as a HOLE.  Reading
through p-aref gives a real undef, and the row now matches perl.

NO PCL_OPT NAME (task #1181's precedent); guard rows are macroexpansions with
negatives.

MEASURED.  Hand-replaced A/B first: `slices` **-33.3 %** against a control pair
at -1.3 % (best-of-9).  SHIPPED, two-core runtime A/B against a `027ba9c`
runtime: **slices -22.2 % / -22.8 %** (2.53x -> 1.95x of perl), best-of-5 and
best-of-7.

BARS: gate (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); twelve slice-READ probe shapes vs perl
5.40.3 identical, including the two ALIASING negatives; guard
`Pl/t/perf-levers-02.t`, inverse-verified.

=== SHIPPED (s470bp-merge resume, 2026-09-06, commit 2ecca3c) ===

The runtime the shutdown had left in scratch/s470bp/rt-L6-AND-L7.lisp was

and gated.

  only the 13 pclxs xs rows (this environment's standing state).
* full perl-tests sweep on the L7 tree: **TOTAL passing 18581 (+0)**, GATE

  bucket to the sweep taken on 485661b before the lever went in.
* companion `--jobs 1` op/hashassign.t op/aassign.t op/list.t op/array.t
  op/hash.t op/local.t, run on BOTH trees: every file reproduces
  baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv, 0 NEW ROW / 0 FIXED ROW / 0 LOST.
* corpus-diff 614c6af IDENTICAL over 111 files, silent drops 5 unchanged;
  emission-ab --shapes --list lib/**/*.pm 27 SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF plus a
  204-file wide leg; ir-host-leak byte-identical to the pre-L7 run;
  PCL_OPT=none byte-identical to main once the preamble's embedded build path
  is normalised (task #217, not this change).
* probe-slice.pl 40/42 vs perl 5.40.3 -- the two misses are #1206's
  scalar-context pair, PRE-EXISTING (the NON-const twin diverges the same way);
  all twelve slice-READ shapes and BOTH aliasing rows identical.
* probe-slice2.pl, run for the FIRST time, 20/20.  Its one reported DIFF is the
  probe file's own shell quoting -- `''` inside `perl -e '...'` closes the
  quote, so PERL ITSELF answers "syntax error near `ne ?`" on that row; run
  from a FILE the dualvar row agrees on both sides; the probe was then repaired (no quote literals at all) and reads 0 divergences of 20.
* PCL_RAW_ELEMS=0 (the all-boxed A/B world): the twelve-shape program is
  byte-identical to perl there too, structurally -- %p-aslice-copy ASKS p-aref
  rather than storing anything itself, so the "a fast path must disappear with
  the gate" trap cannot apply to it.
* guard Pl/t/perf-levers-02.t 11 -> 17 rows: two macroexpansions
  (%p-aslice-copy / %p-hslice-copy), THREE negatives (a foreach over a slice
  keeps `(p-aslice ...)` -- the non-vacuous one, since p-foreach is itself a
  macro; a printed slice keeps it; and the alias-building call is still what
  the foreach walks) and a twelve-shape RUN row.  INVERSE-VERIFIED on a
  485661b tree: rows 12, 13 and 17 fail there, row 17's failing line being the
  `exists $v[3]` divergence this lever fixes (`N` on the base, perl says `E`).
* A/B re-confirmation (NOT the quiet re-measure, which is the reviewer's):
  A 0.1694 s vs B(485661b) 0.2153 s, B/A +27.1 % best-of-7 at load 4.6 with a
  sibling agent running -- the same size as the -22.2 % / -22.8 % at the stop.
